answers.a: The latest major changes to the laws and regulations governing civil service functioning in Senegal are as follows: (1) In August 2024, the Ministry of Public Service launched the drafting process for a new General Statute of the Civil Service, with a four-day workshop to examine the initial draft ('draft 0') of the bill. This reform, anchored in Decree No. 2024-962 of 8 April 2024, aims to unify and modernize the legal framework for both state and territorial civil service and marks a shift to results-based management. (2) Decree No. 2023-678 of 23 March 2023 established a particular statute for the cadre of legal affairs civil servants, grouping them into five corps and specifying recruitment and classification rules. (3) Decree No. 2023-693 of 23 March 2023 reorganized the Ministry of Public Service and Transformation of the Public Sector, creating new directorates and expanding its missions. (4) Decree No. 2022-1815 of 26 September 2022 and Decree No. 2022-1777 of 17 September 2022 expanded and redistributed the Ministry's attributions and formalized its creation. (5) Law No. 2022-08 of 19 April 2022 defined parapublic sector entities as part of the broader public sector. The foundational law, Law No. 61-33 of 15 June 1961, remains in force but is expected to be replaced by the new general statute currently under preparation.

answers.a: Senegal is implementing a comprehensive set of ongoing reforms to improve the civil service recruitment process. The centerpiece is the drafting of a new General Civil Service Statute, with a four-day workshop in August 2024 examining the initial draft. This reform aims to unify and modernize recruitment rules for both state and territorial civil services, shifting towards results-based management. National consultations involving civil society, professional organizations, and public administration stakeholders are informing the reform process. The Ministry has also digitalized recruitment through an online application platform (https://emploi-fpublique.sec.gouv.sn), matching candidates to ministry needs based on various criteria. Institutional strengthening includes the creation of the Direction de la Gestion prévisionnelle des Effectifs, des Emplois et des Compétences (DGEEC) with a dedicated Division du Recrutement, responsible for identifying HR needs and managing recruitment. Additionally, the dematerialization of HR procedures, such as grade advancement commissions, is being extended to all civil servants, supporting the broader modernization and professionalization of public HR management.

The unified file is based on a single-writer/multiple-readers principle for each data type, which enhances data quality, reliability, and real-time accessibility, and reduces duplication and inconsistency. The reform aims to give the State greater control over workforce numbers and the wage bill, ensure coherent data tracking between central and sectoral systems, and support more advanced management solutions. These efforts directly address previous recommendations to rationalize fragmented databases and introduce biometric identification, as highlighted in earlier PEFA assessments.

This reform has the following key features:

1. **Consolidated personnel database**: A single, shared data management system integrating personnel data currently dispersed across multiple structures.
2. **Integration with the payroll system** (*système de gestion de la solde des agents de la fonction publique*), the public finance management system, the pension management system, sectoral HR systems, and the national ID card system.
3. **Data quality improvement**: The objective is to make personnel data reliable, available, and accessible in real time ('rendre fiables, disponibles et accessibles en temps réel les données du personnel').
